observations: Files I read: the whole script request, 1730 lines read in two parts (1-1324 and 1325-1730), fingerprint 2656c857.... It covers the cast, style, continuity, all 9 sections and all 7 pages / 27 panels with their production hands and props. I read both listed files in full: original.txt (hash 78b77a0f...) and source-coverage.json (hash 12dfb5f8...). I also read REVISION-2026-11-11.md and the previous response script-all-r19.json, which I used for the format and earlier issues. I grepped workflow.json and confirmed it carries the same two changed lines: line 1031 has the 03-1 caption and line 1634 has the 04-2 nurse line. I did not otherwise diff workflow.json against the request snapshot. I opened no images, because the request lists none and this is a text stage. readingReview is not required for the script stage.

Reading order: I read the source first. Then I reread the lettering of pages 2-4 on its own, in panel order, without filling gaps from the source. The goal was to check that the new lines make sense on the page alone.

Dialogue matches the source word for word in all 27 panels. I compared every panel against original.txt lines 14-52. For every entry, the textColumns join back into the text field exactly. This includes the new 03-1 columns ('A later morning: ' + 'patients can always check ' + 'in at the front desk.') and the new 04-2 nurse columns ('Hi, Ravi! Just relax ' + 'your arm for me.').

Speakers: captions use narration, on-screen labels use label, 04-2 uses nurse (in the cast), and ananya, meera and ravi speak as named in the source. Panels with two entries keep source order: 03-5, 04-1, 04-3 and 07-4 put the caption before the label, and 04-2 puts the caption before the nurse. Lines the source does not specify are supplements that name things, and the coverage file records them: the WELBUK PRACTICE, CARE and HEALTH labels and the repeated WELBUK VISION in 07-3. No turns are merged across different speakers. The only split is 01-2, where one Meera line becomes two balloons by the same speaker at the ellipsis.

Page 2 -> 3 boundary: 02-4 takes place in the evening office (onboarding section: 'Later the same week, after hours'), and its after says 'ready to see patients with Welbuk (page 3)'. 03-1 has transition.kind time-change, with the bridge 'Morning light at the now-tidy reception after the evening onboarding on page 2'. The new caption now states the time out loud ('A later morning:'). The reception section summary starts with the same phrase. The setting change from paper registers and desk phone to monitor, QR stand and TV is set up by the onboarding.

Other transitions: 03-5 -> 04-1 is a stated short wait (three rows become one highlighted row). 04-2 -> 04-3 is a place change with a panel-level section override to consultation. 04-3 -> 05-1: the tablet is put away and the room is identified as the one in 04-3. 05-4 -> 06-1 is a place change back to reception. 06-4 has a departure override. 07-1 is a time change to a hypothetical 'Tomorrow... may'. 07-2 and 07-3 are vision panels, flagged in continuity with a vignette. 07-4 has transition kind return.

Prop chains: ravi-phone connects at every step from 03-3 to 07-1. It is in his right hand (03-3), then both hands (03-4), his right hand (03-5), being tucked into his pocket (04-1), in his pocket (04-2), out again in 06-1, both hands (06-2), his left hand (06-3, 06-4) and his lap (07-1). The shoulder-bag chain connects from 03-3 to 06-4: shoulder, lap, shoulder, floor, shoulder, floor, shoulder. Raman's walking stick stays in his right hand in 03-1 and 03-5. Priya's phone stays in her left hand in 03-2 and 03-5. The doctor-tablet appears only in 04-3 and is put away in the drawer from 05-1 on. The closed laptop recurs in 04-3 and 05-1 to 05-3. The staff-phone recurs in 02-3, 02-4 and 07-4.

Costume continuity: each section's costumes repeat Ananya's teal kurta, open white coat and stethoscope worn around her neck but not in use. Meera has her blue kurta and the silver bangle on her right wrist. Ravi has his light green shirt and the watch on his left wrist. The nurse wears lavender scrubs and a blank lanyard. Raman and Priya match their sheets in 03-1, 03-2 and 03-5. The specialist, partner and child appear only in vision.

The new 03-1 line read on its own works. 'patients can always check in at the front desk' introduces 'check in' before 03-2's 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app'. 'Some' now clearly contrasts with that, and 03-5's 'Every check-in' gathers all three routes.

The new 04-2 line read on its own works. The caption 'A quick vitals check first.' is followed by the nurse's 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' This no longer repeats the caption. 'your arm' refers to the cuff on his left upper arm described in the scene. Her knowing his name comes from the check-in in 03-3 to 03-4 and the slot in 04-1. The production moment, the nurse about to squeeze the bulb and smiling, fits the line.

Cosmetic, no change required: 'Hi' greets Ravi while the cuff is already on his arm. That is a small timing compression, but natural for a single panel. An English reader could take 'A later morning' as 'late morning', but the indefinite article makes 'a subsequent morning' the more natural reading. The storyboard and lettering reviews should check that it reads as a time cue. The textColumns line 'patients can always check ' is the longest column in 03-1, so caption room should be checked on the new layout.

Carried over for the artwork and lettering stages (not script defects): 04-2 puts the cuff, the oximeter and the wristwatch all on the left arm, so the artwork review should check they stay distinct. The doctor-tablet section text still reaches the 05-2 to 05-4 prompts, so the artwork review should confirm no tablet is drawn there. No panel image was checked in this review.

panels.observation: The source P1 Panel 1 caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' is word for word as narration. It introduces Ananya and depends on no earlier text.

Meera's source line 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups... I wish everything were easier to manage!' is word for word, split at the ellipsis into two balloons by the same speaker. No other speaker's turn sits between them. The registers and phone in the scene set up the list.
Ananya's 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.' is word for word. 'the rest' refers to Meera's list in 01-2, just before it.

The caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' is word for word. The 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' label is a supplement naming the product the source panel describes, and it reads after the caption. The transition is a time change to the evening office.
Ananya's 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' is word for word. 'here' refers to the laptop shown in 02-1.
Meera's 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' is word for word. 'And' follows Ananya's 02-2 line directly with no gap. The WELBUK CARE label is a supplement.
Ananya's 'One team. Better coordination.' is word for word. It sums up 02-2 and 02-3, and Meera answers with a nod, not an added line.

The revised P3 Panel 1 caption 'A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.' is word for word (original.txt line 25). It now introduces 'check in' before 03-2 and states the time change from the evening onboarding in 02-4. The scene of Meera checking in Mr. Raman carries 'front desk'. There is no spoken line to depend on.
The caption 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' is word for word. 'Some' now contrasts with 'patients ... at the front desk' in 03-1.
The caption 'Ravi scans the QR code at the door.' is word for word and names Ravi for the first time. The QR stand in the scene backs 'at the door'.
The caption 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' is word for word. 'his' refers to Ravi in 03-3, and the consent tick-box in the scene shows the consent. No personal data is shown.

The caption 'Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.' and the label 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12' are word for word, in source order. 'Every check-in' gathers the three routes in 03-1 to 03-4, and the three seated patients match the three slots.
The caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' and the label 'NOW · A-12' are word for word, in order. 'his' refers to Ravi, who is standing. A-12 was set up in 03-5.

The caption 'A quick vitals check first.' and the revised nurse line 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' are word for word (original.txt line 33), caption first, speaker nurse. The line no longer repeats the caption. 'your arm' refers to the cuffed arm in the scene. The name is justified by the check-in and slot. 'first' sets up the doctor beat in 04-3 and 05-1. No readings are shown.

The caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' and the label 'RAVI · READY' are word for word, in order. 'he' refers to Ravi in 04-2. The place change is stated, and the tablet appears only here.
Ananya's 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' is word for word. Her knowing his name is grounded in 04-3. The question is answered in 05-2. The tablet is recorded as put away.
Ravi's 'I've been feeling tired lately.' is word for word and answers the 05-1 question directly. It is a routine concern with no diagnosis.

The caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' is word for word. The doctor listens in silence between Ravi's statement and her reply. The only technology in the scene is the closed laptop.
Ananya's 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' is word for word. 'your concerns' refers back to 05-2. It gives no treatment advice.

Meera's 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' is word for word. Welbuk Health was set up in 03-2. The phone comes out of his pocket, where it has been since 04-1.

Ravi's 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' is word for word. 'So' draws on Meera's 06-1 statement, just before it. The WELBUK HEALTH label is a supplement, and no vignette is asked for here.
Meera's 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' is word for word. 'That' answers the 06-2 question, and 'what is available' keeps the source's hedge.
The caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' is word for word. It closes the visit after the 06-3 walkthrough, with the departure section override.
The caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' is word for word. The conditional 'may' keeps it hypothetical, and the transition is a time change.

The 'WELBUK VISION' label the source asks for and the caption 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' are word for word. The continuity text asks for the vignette on 07-2.
The repeated WELBUK VISION label is a supplement that keeps the vision framing. The caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' is word for word.

The labels 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health' and the final caption 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.' are word for word, in source order. The labels link back to 02-1, 02-3 and 06-2. The transition returns to the present.
